newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta trades in tight range despite bono slump.
newsitem.headline: Peseta trades in tight range despite bono slump.

text.p: The peseta remained in a narrow range against the mark in late trade on Friday despite a tumble in bonos, the lira and the dollar, and dealers said the Bank of Spain was probably still propping up the Spanish currency.
"The mark is well offered at 84.90 pesetas and it appears very probable that the Bank of Spain is buying pesetas," one dealer said.
By 1620 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.95/97 per mark compared with 84.88/90 earlier in the session and 84.77/80 late on Thursday.

Dealers said they believed the Bank of Spain had been buying pesetas against the mark at around 84.85/90 earlier in the session. However, they could not quantify the intervention. The Bank of Spain does not comment on its intervention policy.
In Italy, dealers said they saw the Bank of Italy selling marks for lire at 998.50 per mark to try to brake the Italian currency's fall through 1,000 per mark.
However, the lira continued to fall and traded at 1000.50/1.00 per mark, its lowest level in three months.
